annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "Earwicker" on page 36 within "The Encounter in Phoenix Park": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. During this Age of Gods phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu

annotations.annotation_text: Swiftian presence "swift" on page 36 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park"): the Dean of St. Patrick's Cathedral haunts this passage within HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. His dual lovers Stella and Vanessa mirror Issy's split personalities, while his savage satire infuses the Age of Gods dream with political and scatological ferocity.
sources: Ehrenpreis, Irvin. Swift: The Man, His Works, and the Age. https://archive.org/details/swiftmanhisworks01ehre
